title: New chat first, with a case picker
goal: The main button is New chat, not New case. A new chat can be tagged with a case so it becomes a case chat (user, 2026-11-15).
for_whom: A practising lawyer whose day is mostly quick questions, some of which belong to a case.

done_check.check: The sidebar's main button reads New chat and opens a new chat; outside a case it starts with no case, inside a case it starts with that case picked. New case is a small + next to Cases in the sidebar (and the dashboard's New case card stays); it opens /cases/new.

The question box of every new chat (the new chat page, a case's new chat page and the dashboard's quick-question box) has a case chip: 'No case' or the case's title. It lists the user's cases, 'No case', and New case (a link to /cases/new).

Picking a case on a new chat's chip lands on that case's new chat page (case sidebar, the case's example questions) with the typed draft kept; picking 'No case' in a case's new chat lands on the plain new chat page with the draft kept. The first question then makes a chat in the picked case (or none), as it does today.

After a chat has started, the chip of a chat with no case does what Move to case does today (the chat goes into the picked case and opens there), and the separate Move to case button is gone. A case chat's chip shows its case and cannot change it.

While an answer streams, its new words fade in (Streamdown's animate, word by word); a stored answer and a reduced-motion system show words with no fade, and the chat still never jumps (chat-stable d1).

The citation open in the source panel is kept in the chat store (per chat); its chip in the answer is solid while it is open, follows Previous/Next in the panel, and goes back to normal on 'All' (a fix: the highlight did not show).
A playbook picked in a question box is kept in the chat store with that box's draft: leaving the page and coming back shows it still picked; sending clears it.

No memory mode in the app: STORAGE and FILE_INDEX are gone (always R2 and Zilliz), and so are PUT /api/files/<id> and putUpload; an upload to a case still reaches Ready. memoryStore and memoryFileIndex stay as unit-test fakes only.

A file's processing states come through the tRPC subscription file.events (GET /api/files/<id>/events is gone): an upload to a case shows its steps live in the tray and on the Files page and reaches Ready; another user's file id is refused; the only plain routes left are /api/chat and the Clerk webhook.

'Open the law' in the source panel opens /doc/<law> in the same tab (Back returns to the chat, an answer still streaming keeps going): the law's text, scrolled to the cited section, beside our stored PDF (or the stored HTML page, in a sandboxed frame) from kb.docs.source_key; on a phone, Text and PDF/Page tabs. No link to the official site's copy. Publish fills source_key (all 7,715 laws backfilled 2026-11-15).

A cited law's timeline in the source panel is a list, oldest first: Enacted, every law that changed any part of it (year and name, capitals made readable), the ones that changed the cited section marked, Today; a header 'Amended by N laws · M changed this section' or 'Never amended'; more than 6 folds the middle behind 'N more'. Fits 390 px with no sideways scroll. (A fix: it showed only the cited section's changes, on a scaled line that overlapped years.)

While an answer streams: a citation not yet closed shows as a 'citing…' chip, never raw [[…]] text; each citation joins the Sources panel under its law as it lands, and the number of sources only grows (no extra group that merges later); the checked / not-verified line updates during the stream. The word fade's spans are not replaced mid-stream.

A law citation's panel reads in a lawyer's order: law, section, in force, Open the law; the cited text; the law's timeline, open and short (year, law, 'changed this section'); then the whole law, folded. No separate 'Amended N times' block, no clauses in the panel.

'Full history' on the panel's timeline opens /history/<law>?c=<section> in the same tab, oldest first: the section as enacted (labelled so, never 'as it stands'), then each change since (date, amending law and its section, what it did, the amending section's whole text, a link to open that law at it), changes after today named, then the whole law's timeline. The source panel has no history of its own: the section's text (labelled 'as enacted in <year>' when amended since), the short timeline with 'Full history', the whole law. No agent-only note ('[truncated: …]'); a wrong or foreign id is a 404.

An amending section's citation (s. 8 of Act No. 26 of 2002) says 'an amending provision' (not 'the text in force'), names what it amends ('Amends s. 22 of Rent (Act No. 7 of 1972)'), and its timeline is the amended law's with this change marked 'this amendment'; its Full history opens the amended section's history.

The panel and the Sources list load a light corpus.chunk (section, which laws changed it, what it amends, the timeline; no clauses, two database round trips); the clauses come only from corpus.history on the history page; the whole law (126 KB for the Rent Act) loads only on 'Read the whole law here'.

While an answer streams in a chat with earlier answers, those answers never re-render (0 DOM changes in them, memo on their parts, no animation) and the page stays smooth: in the rent chat (3 earlier answers) the longest main-thread block is under 200 ms (was 439 ms) and the Sources list adds each citation without a request.

'Jump to latest' is a solid round icon button (no text, not transparent, labelled for screen readers); it and the follow-along while streaming glide to the end (eased, about 0.6 s from the top of a long chat), stop when the lawyer scrolls up, and jump instantly under reduced motion.
At 390 px the sidebar's New chat and the chip fit without horizontal scroll and the chip's list is usable; app checks pass (biome, typecheck, unit tests).

scenarios.steps: On the dashboard, type 'Can a landlord evict a tenant without a court order?', pick the Perera v. Silva case on the chip, send.
scenarios.expect: The question is still in the box after the pick, on the case's page; the answer comes in a chat listed under that case and reasons with the case's facts.

scenarios.steps: Click New chat in the sidebar, ask a plain question about the Rent Act, then put the chat into a case from the chip.
scenarios.expect: The chat starts with no case; after the pick it opens inside the case and the next answer uses the case's facts.

scenarios.steps: Inside a case, click New chat, switch the chip to 'No case', ask a question.
scenarios.expect: The chat is a plain chat, listed with the other chats outside cases, not under the case.

out_of_scope: Opening the PDF at the cited section's page (needs pages per chunk: a full ETL rebuild, later).
A chat in more than one case.
Moving a case chat to another case, or taking it out of its case.
Making a case from inside the chip (New case links to the page, as today).

decisions.note: Reverses 2026-10-27 'chat outside a case stays, second': New chat is the main action, the case is one pick away (user).

New case: a small + by Cases; chip in the question box; picking a case navigates into the case with the draft; inside a case New chat starts in that case; chip on every new-chat box; after start it only puts a no-case chat into a case; New case in the chip is a link (user).
Added during the preview: Streamdown's streaming animation in answers (user). Fade-in by word, 200 ms; blurIn, slideUp and a caret are its other options.

Added during the preview: the open citation's chip highlight was broken; the selection now lives in the zustand chat store (user), and each chip subscribes to it, so a block Streamdown keeps still updates.

Sources list slow while streaming: measured, not compute (citation parse 0.017 ms per token over 37k chars) but a corpus.chunk request per citation (0.8-2 s each), which the list waited for. The agent's search/read/asOf results are already in the browser (this chat: 90 sections with law, title, path, text), so the list groups from them; only a citation the tools never returned is looked up.
